faq: Do I need an Etsy account first?

Not if you tick the start-from-scratch box. You open the account yourself, because Etsy needs your identity and bank details, and we guide each step. Then you add us as a shop manager and we do the rest.
Can you enter my bank details?
No. You type bank, tax and identity details yourself, because they are private and Etsy verifies them. We walk you through where each item goes and check the rest of the settings.
Will you choose my shop name?
We give you a shortlist of names that read well, are short and look free to use as an Etsy name. You choose. We also point out if a name looks close to a registered brand.
Etsy charges you directly: a listing fee for each item, a transaction fee on sales and a payment processing fee. Our price is for the setup work only, and we explain each fee on the checklist.
desc:
Etsy shop setup and launch checklist work takes you from an empty account to a shop that is ready for its first sale. Ecom Swift LLC sets up your Etsy shop in your own account, covering the name, sections, policies, shipping and opening-day tasks.

## What is Etsy shop setup?

Etsy shop setup is the one-time work of opening a seller account properly: choosing a shop name, filling in the shop details, creating sections, writing policies, configuring shipping and payments and preparing the first listings. Each step is simple alone, but there are many of them and the order matters.

Ecom Swift LLC walks through them with you. You keep the account and the login, and we work inside it from your direction.

## Why a careful start saves trouble later

A shop opened in a hurry often carries small problems for months. A name that is hard to spell, policies copied from somewhere else, a shipping profile that charges too little, sections that do not match the products. Changing these after orders arrive means more work and sometimes confused buyers.

Starting with a plan also reduces stress. Opening a shop involves personal and financial details, and many new sellers stall at the payment screen or the policy page. A clear checklist makes each step smaller.

## How a good launch affects the first sales

New shops have little history, so every detail has to build trust. A clean name, a complete About section, clear policies and well-made first listings tell shoppers the shop is serious. Sections help visitors find what they want quickly, and correct shipping settings prevent unpleasant surprises at checkout.

Setup also affects how fast you can start learning. When the basics are right, you can spend your time watching which items get views and improving them, instead of fixing mistakes. Launch results depend on your products, prices and the market, so we focus on a solid foundation rather than promises.

## What a launch-ready Etsy shop includes

- A shortlist of shop names, checked for availability on Etsy.
- Shop details, location, language and currency filled in.
- Sections that group your products in a way buyers understand.
- Policies for shipping, returns and custom orders written for your shop.
- A shipping profile with processing time and rates in the larger packages.
- An About section and shop announcement.
- A shop icon sized and uploaded.
- The first listings created, ready to publish.
- A launch checklist and a plan for launch week.

## What we do

We begin with a short brief about what you sell. We prepare a list of name options and check which are available, and you choose. Then we set up the shop details and sections and write policies that match how you really work.

In Standard, we add your first listings, a shipping profile, a shop announcement and an icon. Premium adds ten listings, a walk-through of payment settings with you on screen, a launch week plan and a handover call. Payment and bank details are always entered by you, and we only guide you through the steps. We finish with a checklist so nothing is forgotten on opening day.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Pick a name that is easy to say and spell.
- Write policies that reflect how you actually work.
- Set realistic processing times from the start.
- Create the first listings with full details and good photos.
- Read the launch checklist before you open the shop.

**Avoid:**
- Copying another seller's policies word for word.
- Choosing a name that closely resembles an existing brand.
- Opening with only one or two thin listings.
- Setting free shipping before you know your costs.
- Sharing your password or bank details with anyone.

## Who this service is for

It suits a first-time seller who has products ready but feels lost in the setup screens. It helps a crafter moving from fairs and local markets to online sales, and a person opening a second shop who wants it set up properly from day one.

## What we need from you

Send a few lines about your products, your preferred shop name ideas and your photos for the first listings. You create the Etsy account, and then you invite us as a manager with limited permissions where Etsy supports it. We never ask for your password, and you handle all payment and bank entries yourself.
